title: OS binding: builtin functions
description: Scripts in scope bound to specific operating systems through Claris builtin functions: curated OS affinity from the official documentation (there is no structured Claris OS table; absence of a statement means 'Claris states nothing', never 'runs everywhere'). Covers 'exclusive' functions (ComputeModel / GetModelAttributes / GetLiveText -> macOS+iOS Core ML, Get(TouchKeyboardState) / Get(TriggerGestureInfo) -> Windows+iOS) and source-true inverse 'unsupported' statements. Behavior variants (path formats, window geometry, ...) are documentation knowledge -> schema-viewer badges only; the platform-detection functions (Get(SystemPlatform), Get(Device), ...) are the guard idiom -> context evidence, never a binding. Includes transitive custom-function wrappers (via CF, cycle-guarded closure); the core metric counts scripts only. 'ios' is the OPERATING SYSTEM (FileMaker Go and iOS SDK apps), never the Go runtime chip. Inventory, not defects - findings are neutral properties, never errors.
author: fm-lab rules

rule.rationale: An OS-bound builtin function binds every calling script (directly or through custom functions) to the operating systems Claris names in the help prose - the runtime compatibility model cannot see this (functions have no compatibility table at all).
rule.remediation: Nothing to fix. Use the inventory to know which scripts assume which OS; guard OS-bound calls with Get(SystemPlatform) checks where a script must run cross-platform.
